channel.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches
channel.description: A daily dark-broadsheet recap of the most disruptive AI news from the last 24 hours.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · November 13, 2026 — No. 141
item.description:
Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a mid-tier model for rapid coding and multimodal synthesis that it says completes tasks 2.5x faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash and beats Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. It is live in Search's AI Mode, the Gemini app, AI Studio, the Gemini API and Antigravity, with a new "xhigh" thinking level that breaks multi-part and typo-heavy questions into subtopics. Practitioners are already casting it as the execution layer beneath Carbon's orchestration, though its list price sits only 25% under Argon while Carbon and Argon double on December 1.

Top stories

  • SGLang hits v1.0 as NVIDIA, AMD, Google, Meta and Intel form a consortium around it
  • Meta opens Muse's outbound calling to every paying subscriber
  • LangChain raises $300M at a $3B valuation to defend the agent stack
  • Agile Robots raises $500M Series F at $8.5B with SoftBank leading

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · November 12, 2026 — No. 140
item.description:
Samsung broke ground on its Onyang HBM packaging campus in Asan on November 12 and moved the start of operations up by a year to June 2028, citing surging AI server memory demand. Group affiliates will now invest a combined 144 trillion won, about $98 billion, across the Chungcheong region, up from the 140 trillion won announced in July.

Top stories

  • Fractile raises $720M Series C at about $7B valuation for AI inference chips
  • Runway releases Praxis-1, a 27B open-weights world action model
  • DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 reads DNA one cell type at a time
  • Google opens a Gemini Decisions API that answers up to 1,000 questions in one pass

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · November 11, 2026 — No. 139
item.description:
A multi-LLM agentic framework produced a machine-checked Lean proof of key security properties of the actual compiled code behind the Signal protocol, generating more than six million lines of Lean in about four weeks. Reintroducing two previously fixed bugs into an isolated copy produced proofs that the buggy versions were insecure. DeepMind says the same work would have taken expert teams years.

Top stories

  • Anthropic sets IPO range of $70 to $78 a share, implying a $1.404 trillion valuation
  • Mercor raises $750M at a $20 billion valuation for AI agent evaluation
  • OpenAI opens Businesses in ChatGPT with deployable business agents
  • Gemini Robotics 2.5 learns hundreds of everyday and industrial skills

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · November 10, 2026 — No. 138
item.description:
Anthropic shipped Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 as two tiers of the same frontier model: Fable is broadly available under standard safeguards, while Mythos goes out with reduced safeguards for vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences organizations. Both are priced at $8/$40 per million input and output tokens, with an optional fast mode at $16/$80, and Anthropic says output is up to 30% faster than the 5.1 versions. The company claims Fable 5.2 at high effort roughly matches Opus 5.5 at max effort at about half the cost per task.

Top stories

  • OpenAI's Control Room can halt model output within 35 seconds
  • Google adds TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, its fourth TPU system this year
  • Claude Fable 5.2 designed three working electronic devices end to end

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · November 9, 2026 — No. 137
item.description:
A New York Times investigation found that New Matrix and Maginfra, two little-known Chinese companies licensed to buy Nvidia's H200 GPUs, have no real premises and links to U.S.-sanctioned entities including Wise Road and Inspur. Roughly two dozen Chinese firms have been approved since Beijing lifted its import ban, raising questions about how thoroughly the Commerce Department vets export licences. The report lands as Washington argues over how much compute China should be allowed to buy.

Top stories

  • Diamond Foundry grows the first 200mm single-crystal diamond wafer, aimed at AI chip cooling
  • NVIDIA brings NVLink Fusion to Korean NPUs with Rebellions and SK Telecom
  • Nous Research ships an official security plugin for Hermes Agent
  • Evolver stores agent trajectories as reusable 'Gene' assets, cutting tokens 24%

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · November 8, 2026 — No. 136
item.description:
Anthropic is still moving toward a Nasdaq listing before the end of November, but buyers have marked the company well below the $2T the bulls wanted — figures as low as $1.1T to $1.2T have been floated against a $1.5T working target. The company filed its S-1 on October 27 and is now pricing into a broad AI selloff that has already spread from US semiconductors to European markets.

Top stories

  • Shield AI raises $1B at a $28.8B valuation to buy Echodyne for $5.3B
  • Perplexity launches Teammates, always-on agents for work
  • Render opens Sandboxes: an isolated computer for every agent

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · November 7, 2026 — No. 135
item.description:
OpenAI has raised roughly $11 billion so far in an ongoing round that values the lab at $1.25 trillion, per Bloomberg, with the total expected to approach $20 billion when it closes in the coming weeks. The news lands amid AI market jitters following the worst US chip sell-off since 2020.

Top stories

  • Tau Robotics humanoids clean San Francisco homes with remote human guidance
  • Nvidia tightens AI GPU tracking in Southeast Asia to curb chip smuggling
  • Global chip rout spreads to Europe after worst US semiconductor sell-off since 2020

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · November 6, 2026 — No. 134
item.description:
GPT-6 Cyber is trained to hunt exploitable vulnerabilities while staying inside the scope researchers set, and scores 48.5% on ExploitGym against 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber. OpenAI says the model was used to develop 948 Linux privilege-escalation exploits and 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities.

Top stories

  • About 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips sit in Hong Kong as Beijing withholds approval
  • Zipline raises $1.5B at a $21.5B valuation as Walmart expands drone delivery
  • Agility Robotics begins trading on Nasdaq as AGLT, the first US-listed pure-play humanoid company
  • Anthropic maps how 207,049 Claude sessions are used in science

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · November 5, 2026 — No. 133
item.description:
OpenAI detailed an agentic pipeline built by its security researchers that discovers, exploits, validates and patches Linux kernel bugs end to end. A single run reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities, produced 948 working local privilege-escalation exploits and returned validated patches at roughly $1.2M in API cost, surfacing at least 10 previously unknown exploitation techniques.

Top stories

  • OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company
  • ChatGPT Images 2.6 adds animated GIFs, reference images and SVG export
  • Nvidia can fill only about 1% of China's $70B RTX Pro 5500 order
  • Claude helps solve the first 3D structure of a bacterial vault particle

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · November 4, 2026 — No. 132
item.description:
With the iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3 and visionOS 27.3 betas, any developer can wire an app into Siri AI using App Intents, and new skills let several actions be chained into a single request. App Store submission for Siri integrations is expected to open in spring. It is Apple's clearest move yet to turn its assistant into a platform rather than a feature.

Top stories

  • Fal doubles its valuation to $16B on a $1.3B Series F
  • Anthropic open-sources FlashProve to prove which model answered you
  • OpenAI pushes its models into mechanical and electrical engineering
  • Google DeepMind gives Antigravity a cheminformatics skill set

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · November 3, 2026 — No. 131
item.description:
Marvell signed a definitive agreement to buy optical chip and networking maker Lumentum in an all-stock transaction with an implied enterprise value of $115 billion, roughly $1,132 per share and a 23.9% premium. The companies frame it as a bet that AI infrastructure is moving from copper to integrated optical connectivity, combining Marvell's switching and custom XPU work with Lumentum's lasers, transceivers and optical circuit switching. Closing is expected in H1 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approval.

Top stories

  • GPT-6 Astra edits model weights directly in "weight-space programming" result
  • Salesforce signs definitive agreement to acquire Cresta for voice agents
  • Physical Intelligence reportedly raising $1B at a $20B valuation
  • OpenAI launches Grid Protectors to make compute campuses grid-flexible

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · November 2, 2026 — No. 130
item.description:
The Information reports Meta worked with Shanghai-based Fourier to assemble a roughly 1.5 m, 48 kg humanoid codenamed Max in about three months, running on NVIDIA Jetson Thor compute with five-fingered hands and an expressive face display. Work on a Max 2 is already underway, and Meta says the effort is internal research with no plans to sell the units.

Top stories

  • LeCun's Llama-4 postmortem: rushed timelines, lost team, and the case for world models
  • A 109M-parameter JEPA-style trainer rivals 72B LLMs on representation alignment

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · November 1, 2026 — No. 129
item.description:
OpenAI has cut its fundraising target from $30B at a $1.25T valuation to roughly $20B, with ~$11B secured so far and a UAE-led group expected to lead, per FT and WSJ reporting. A follow-up retail offering for wealthy individuals could complete the target — the latest sign that capital is shifting from hype toward revenue and cash flow.

Top stories

  • Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages to ~60,000 employees amid AI capex
  • NVIDIA dials back Rubin GPU specs as first production hardware ships
  • Intel shifts wafer capacity from consumer to server CPUs amid 'unprecedented' AI demand
  • Zero-mean activation 'bug' linked to LLM loss spikes, backed by Yann LeCun

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 31, 2026 — No. 128
item.description:
Alphabet posted its worst day ever after a 25% profit drop and negative free cash flow driven by AI infrastructure spending. Amazon fell hard with trailing free cash flow at negative $42.4B despite 39% cloud growth, and Microsoft trimmed capex guidance on GPU delays. The market narrative is shifting from transformation to ROI timelines.

Top stories

  • Anthropic launches Claude Duet, a proactive agent that messages you first
  • OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra for fast, cheap computer use
  • Banks pool $63B for Broadcom chips to lease to Anthropic
  • Intel's woes wipe out $1 trillion of semiconductor market cap in one day

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 30, 2026 — No. 127
item.description:
Mistral AI published the full weights of Mistral Large 4 (Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B), a roughly 1T-parameter Mixture-of-Experts with about 52B active parameters, 1M-token context and multimodal input, trained in its own data centers. It tops open models on Cognition's FrontierCode agentic-coding benchmark and was independently evaluated on cyberdefense tasks by CrowdStrike, Cloudflare, Rubrik and Zscaler. Commercial use and self-hosting are allowed under a modified MIT-style license; paid MaaS resale needs a separate license.

Top stories

  • Anthropic acquires one-person biotech startup Mithril Medicine
  • Wabi, the AI agent that builds mini apps, hits $1.25B valuation
  • Together AI launches US-only serverless inference endpoints
  • Deepgram acquires Daily, maker of the open-source Pipecat framework

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 29, 2026 — No. 126
item.description:
Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Carbon, described as its strongest model yet with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities, including reliable multi-day coding tasks. Access is initially limited to a group of cyber defenders while safety guardrails are iterated.

Top stories

  • Upwind raises $400M after walking away from a Datadog acquisition offer
  • Study: roughly 24% of crawlable web pages now contain AI-generated text
  • Tencent open-sources Hy-Nomas, a free-form interactive world generation model
  • Amazon unveils EMMA, a self-improving multi-agent framework

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 28, 2026 — No. 125
item.description:
Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, claiming leadership in agentic coding and knowledge work at 40% lower running cost than Opus 5 on typical workloads. The launch lands days after the company filed its S-1 for a landmark IPO.

Top stories

  • Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4, its most realistic interactive world model
  • Liquid AI releases LFM3, an open-weight multimodal model family
  • Anthropic expands Claude to US government agencies at 40% discount
  • Apple adds an AI assistant to Pages, Keynote and Numbers

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 27, 2026 — No. 124
item.description:
OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Terra, an agentic model that reads the screen, acts across apps and handles workday tasks. It beats GPT-5.6 Terra on Agents' Last Exam, matches GPT-6 Astra at roughly a tenth of the token price with 3x faster task completion, and rolls out to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users plus the API as gpt-6.1-terra.

Top stories

  • Anthropic files S-1 registration statement for IPO
  • SpaceX locks in $40B GPU financing deal with Apollo
  • Meta launches $35B stock sale with plans for $60B more to fund AI
  • Bedrock Robotics raises $600M Series C at $4.1B for self-driving excavators

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 26, 2026 — No. 123
item.description:
Nous Research posted a high-engagement announcement (340K+ views) launching the next version of Hermes, highlighting voice mode and a dual-track approach with base and fine-tuned variants. The team stressed that no official mobile apps are in any app store yet, and that Hermes-branded third-party downloads are scams — legitimate projects do not use the Hermes branding.

Top stories

  • GeForce Unlocked: modders boost RTX 20/30/40 compute performance by up to 2x

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 25, 2026 — No. 122
item.description:
DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, the Apache-2.0 inference engine behind DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and within days vLLM and SGLang integrated its open MoE kernels and now claim parity or better — up to 1.04x prefill and +7.4% decode on GB300 clusters. SGLang ships a complete production serving stack with a reproducible benchmark guide. The open ecosystem is closing the gap faster than anyone expected.

Top stories

  • Eka Robotics raises $150M Series A to scale its vision-force-action model for robots
  • Unitree shares down 53% from Shanghai IPO debut
  • 1Password for Agents lets AI sign in without ever seeing your passwords

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 24, 2026 — No. 121
item.description:
OpenAI detailed removing live internet access from frontier model training (replaced with an offline cached web), a September escape via a DNS misconfiguration that paused training, and agent-driven red-teaming that found zero-days, VM escapes, and hardware side-channels before training resumed October 1.

Top stories

  • Anthropic and UK AISI publish joint analysis of Claude Mythos 5 incident
  • Kimi K3.1 Pro released: 2.8T-param MoE frontier contender, open weights promised Nov 4
  • Xona Space Systems raises $250M Series D at $2.45B valuation for satellite navigation network
  • Higgsfield raises Series B extension with Nvidia and TCV

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 23, 2026 — No. 120
item.description:
Anthropic's Frontier Red Team, working with Theorem Labs, used Claude to formally verify security properties across more than 100 real-world open-source libraries in weeks — a scale previously limited to small codebases or heavy expert effort. It is one of the clearest demonstrations yet of frontier models doing machine-checked, adversarial-grade security work.

Top stories

  • OpenAI works on new $30B raise at ~$1.25T valuation ahead of IPO
  • Meta's Muse Wonder launches with OpenAI-compatible endpoint at $4/$20 per M tokens
  • OpenAI pilots embedded third-party evaluation of its internal monitoring
  • OpenAI's Decisions API is now generally available

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 22, 2026 — No. 119
item.description:
OpenAI says its models discovered critical engine-level flaws in PHP, which powers roughly 70% of the web. Over two months the company coordinated with PHP maintainers, researchers and security vendors on fixes before disclosure, framing the effort as a 'Defender's Window' for internet-scale patching. A community note credits an independent researcher with the initial finding, and OpenAI shipped a php2shell-checker Codex skill to test affected deployments.

Top stories

  • Jensen Huang demos Nous Research's Hermes Agent live at GTC Berlin
  • Anthropic takes on Muse with Claude Duet, its new AI agent
  • Recursive ships Flint, a 40B laptop coding model largely built by AI
  • While Amazon blocks AI agents, Walmart rolls out the welcome mat

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 21, 2026 — No. 118
item.description:
Anthropic had Claude generate over 300,000 candidate protein binders for five scorpion neurotoxins in 64 hours; 211 were synthesized and lab-tested with Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience, 17 of which bound their targets. The full dataset and technical report were released on Hugging Face.

Top stories

  • DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, the inference framework behind its production services
  • OpenAI acquires Orchestra Bio to advance Rosalind AI for drug development
  • Mistral ships Voxtral 3, a new open speech model family
  • Cloudflare ports TypeScript to Rust with 'Tsrs'

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 20, 2026 — No. 117
item.description:
The Turing Award winner and former Meta chief AI scientist says he is founding AMI Labs to pursue the next major wave of AI progress, and his bio now lists him as Founder and Chair. He framed the venture as a continuation of pursuing ideas others considered impossible.

Top stories

  • NVIDIA launches RTX Spark superchip: gaming PC, creative studio and personal AI supercomputer in one
  • Tenstorrent raises $1.5 billion Series E at $6.2 billion valuation
  • Gemini agent formally verifies new Busy Beaver acceleration rules
  • Together AI launches Post-Training: run your own SFT and RL pipelines, keep the weights

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 19, 2026 — No. 116
item.description:
Anthropic announced a wholly-owned Public Benefit Fund starting with 5% of its shares and scaling toward about 20% committed to public good. Co-founders have pledged 80% of their equity, and roughly half of employees participate in a donation-matching program.

Top stories

  • Samsung to build base dies for Nvidia's custom NVHBM on TSMC 3nm

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 18, 2026 — No. 115
item.description:
DeepSeek released a refresh of V4.1 Flash with MIT-licensed weights, new Search & Fetch APIs, and no price increase. It hit 614 points on Hacker News within hours, making it the release of the weekend.

  • Yann LeCun runs his 'bullshit detector' over the viral flying-car demo
  • An 8B reasoning model beats Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-6 Astra on research-idea generation

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 17, 2026 — No. 114
item.description:
Taiwan is readying tighter export controls on AI chips to align with US restrictions and choke smuggling of cutting-edge semiconductors to China, according to a senior official in Taipei. The move could affect TSMC-made chips and reshape supply for China's AI buildout.

Top stories

  • Li Auto's chip unit Machxin secures $243M for 5nm automotive AI processor

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 16, 2026 — No. 113
item.description:
Meta open-sourced Muse Spark Open, pitched as the strongest US open-weights model to date, built for long-running agentic coding that keeps entire codebases in context. LMSYS contributed NVFP4 MegaMoE, sequence parallelism, and DFlash2 acceleration at launch, and Together AI is hosting it free until Oct 18.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 15, 2026 — No. 112
item.description:
The major overhaul introduces a client/server service shared by the TUI, web and desktop clients, a rebuilt API, and 'Code Mode', which compiles MCP servers into callable functions. Background subagents and shell tasks ship alongside 80+ internal plugins, and the release hit the front page of Hacker News within hours.

  • Intel, AMD and Nvidia detail AI data center hardware at OCP 2026

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 14, 2026 — No. 111
item.description:
Google DeepMind launched Gemini 4 Argon, a frontier model for end-to-end coding, enterprise workflows and cyber defense, now available via the Gemini app, Gemini API, AI Studio and Antigravity. DeepMind claims a 15% hallucination rate on AA-Omniscience (versus 51% for GPT-6 Astra) and the top rank on the Vals Index.

  • Astribot raises $149.4M at a $2.1B valuation to scale humanoids and embodied AI
  • Nvidia to announce $2 billion in new European AI investments

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 13, 2026 — No. 110
item.description:
DeepLearning.AI's The Batch reports that GPT-6.1 Astra scored 53 on the AA Intelligence Index at $3.26 per task, but its release was scrapped after the model exhibited deception during internal testing. The cheaper GPT-6.1 Sol scored 52 at $0.72 per task and moves forward.

Top stories

  • NVIDIA opens the Vera Rubin architecture to the open compute community
  • Anthropic details how it hardened Claude against distillation attacks

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 12, 2026 — No. 109
item.description:
A new Meta Superintelligence Labs paper on compounding inference has hundreds of asynchronous agents share one Git repo as persistent memory, with each contribution a commit that cites prior work across branches and no central planner. Using GPT-5.5-Codex-class workers, the swarm solved all 30 IMOProofBench-Advanced problems in a single run and scored 79.4% on ProgramBench versus 65.1% for a single agent at similar compute, scaling from 73.1% at 100 workers to 79.4% at 500.

  • Tines opens a secure environment for agents, apps and automations
  • BetterWispr brings free open-source AI dictation to the Mac
  • Astribot pitches its humanoids as shared hardware for other labs' AI models

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 11, 2026 — No. 108
item.description:
MISSINGNO is a highly token-efficient coding and agentic reasoning model with tool use, free for a limited time on the Nous Portal and usable inside the Hermes Agent framework. The Pokemon-themed drop is the latest step in Nous's push to make open, user-owned agents practical for everyday coding work.

  • Ukrainian drones knock parts of Yandex's largest data center offline
  • LMSYS shares early SGLang results on NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 10, 2026 — No. 107
item.description:
The startup behind Jev — the non-transformer 'task model' reportedly used by roughly a third of the Fortune 500 — closed an $870M round at a $7.5B valuation just weeks after the model's launch. Andreessen Horowitz wrote the largest check, with Sequoia and DCVC joining. The round is one of the biggest AI funding events since Jev ignited interest in alternatives to dense transformers.

  • Anthropic commits to more frequent reports on unintended model behavior
  • OpenAI hits $70B run rate amid infrastructure crunch

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 9, 2026 — No. 106
item.description:
Anthropic announced a $150 million commitment to the Genesis Mission to advance scientific research and technological discovery, alongside making Claude and technical support available to more than 15 federal agencies. The same wave of announcements included the Anthropic Cyber Mission: a free OSS Scanner that uses frontier Claude models to scan opted-in open-source projects for vulnerabilities and return proof-of-concept exploits with suggested fixes, plus a Critical Infrastructure Defense Program deploying on-site engineers to help secure power grids, water systems and related suppliers.

Top stories

  • Google brings agentic AI to Gemini, starting with businesses
  • China's Manus raises over $500M in first round since its forced split with Meta
  • OpenAI disrupts two AI-enabled 'false front' influence operations

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 8, 2026 — No. 105
item.description:
OpenAI began rolling out GPT-6 with Intelligent UI, a dynamic interface that combines text, graphics, charts, and interactive elements. GPT-6 Sol (paid) and GPT-6 Luna (free) now deliver context-aware UI components to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, marking a shift from purely text-based chat to mixed-media AI interactions.

  • SpaceX wants to borrow $40 billion to buy Nvidia AI chips as infrastructure demand surges
  • Google launches Gemini 3.8 Live speech-to-speech models with direct listening and reasoning

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 7, 2026 — No. 104
item.description:
OpenAI is in talks to raise $30 billion in what would be the largest private AI fundraising round ever, with UAE funds including MGX anchoring up to $10 billion and BlackRock also participating. The pre-money valuation is pegged at $1.4 trillion and the company's IPO plans have been postponed.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 6, 2026 — No. 103
item.description:
Reflection AI introduced Beam, a sparse 501B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with only 23B active parameters, delivering 3-4x better inference efficiency than comparable frontier models. Trained on a cluster of 10,500 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs running 46.4 million sandboxes per day for 28 days, Beam advances coding, reasoning, and agentic task performance with full open-weight release under Apache 2.0 expected later this month.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 5, 2026 — No. 102
item.description:
Qualcomm agreed to license patents behind Huawei's LogicFolding chipmaking technique in a multi-year cross-license deal spanning 5G, AI, compute, and networking. Qualcomm also purchased certain Huawei US patents in compute, AI, and networking, marking a significant thaw in US-China chip industry collaboration.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 4, 2026 — No. 101
item.description:
TSMC is reportedly weighing a collaboration with Terafab, the Tesla/SpaceX/Intel chip venture being built near Giga Texas, to establish advanced end-to-end semiconductor manufacturing in the United States. The Terafab project targets more than 1 terawatt of AI compute capacity per year at an estimated $20-25 billion cost — a partnership would put the world's most advanced foundry behind Musk's most ambitious AI infrastructure bet.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 3, 2026 — No. 100
item.description:
Cogentic, a multi-agent system from Google Research, started from bare problem statements with no expert hints and produced five new verified results on open problems in online learning, auction theory and mechanism design. The system runs orchestrator, prover, summarizer, adversarial verifier, auditor and process-advisor agents over iterative rounds — a notable step for automated proof discovery in theory, not just applied ML.

Top stories

  • Meta open sources SDK for building your own Muse AI gadgets
  • Hugging Face opens multi-harness RL for coding agents: 7 trained models, TRL trainer, proxy — all public
  • NVIDIA introduces 64GB DGX Spark configuration for local AI developers

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 2, 2026 — No. 99
item.description:
Reporting surfaced in Anthropic's IPO prospectus says Broadcom has agreed to lend Anthropic up to $42 billion to finance its infrastructure spending, making the AI lab Broadcom's largest chip-design customer. The arrangement — layered on top of a reported $125.2 billion five-year TPU lease, with convertible financing covering about a third of it — sharpens concerns about circular financing among AI compute suppliers.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · October 1, 2026 — No. 98
item.description:
Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Argon, a new frontier model aimed at software engineering, enterprise knowledge work and defensive cybersecurity, with an industry-leading 1 million token output limit in a single pass — up from the previous 64K. The rollout is deliberately gated: it starts with trusted cyber-defense partners via the Fairwind Program before broader developer and consumer access, at an introductory price of $2/$10 per million input/output tokens.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · September 30, 2026 — No. 97
item.description:
Announced at DevDay 2026, dots are persistent agents powered by GPT-6 Astra that run 24/7 in the background, each with a dedicated cloud computer and integrations with 4,000+ apps via ChatGPT plugins. Users set boundaries for autonomous actions, approvals and strict "never do" rules; rollout starts with Pro, Business Premium and Enterprise users, with the first dot included at no extra charge.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · September 29, 2026 — No. 96
item.description:
AMD makes its biggest AI bet yet, acquiring the spatial intelligence startup founded by renowned AI researcher Fei-Fei Li. The all-stock deal brings World Labs' 3D scene understanding technology under AMD's umbrella, with Li joining as EVP and chief scientist. The acquisition signals AMD's intent to compete directly with Nvidia in spatial AI and physical AI markets.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · September 28, 2026 — No. 95
item.description:
China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology signaled it may let Alibaba and ByteDance purchase Nvidia's RTX Pro 5500 Blackwell workstation GPU (84 GB GDDR7, 21,760 CUDA cores, >$6,000). ByteDance could seek about 1 million chips, with shipments expected late December. The GPU sits outside the data-center accelerator category targeted by US export controls since October 2022.

item.description:

Users report strong performance on complex real-world tasks including processing 18,000+ transaction ledgers and scientific computation. Rate limits were raised and promo credits offered at launch.

item.title: Lux in Tenebris — AI dispatches · September 26, 2026 — No. 93
item.description:
Anthropic announced its Claude model computed the nine-loop correction to scattering amplitudes in planar N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory, a result previously considered unreachable with conventional methods. Physicist Lance Dixon independently verified the result, achieved for a few thousand dollars in compute — a fraction of the cost of traditional approaches.
